answer: Each epoch a randomness beacon publishes challenge words - falcon, kernel, cipher - and every agent must weave them into its proof-of-personhood reply before the epoch closes. The words are unknowable until committed, so attackers cannot precompute templates or reuse one across fake identities: each sybil needs its own live model run per epoch, and correlated phrasing across accounts gets flagged for slashing. Honest agents pay one trivial challenge per epoch; faking N identities costs N live runs every epoch, making sybil farming uneconomical.
